pattern: segments() and copyElements(minimumCapacity:) expose up to two contiguous spans
complexity: O(n) copy; O(1) auxiliary words excluding mandatory destination; same retained long[] geometry
rationale: Use System.arraycopy in one private atom; keep power-of-two capacity and primitive throwing/iterator contracts; no Swift ownership layer

pattern: UInt words; population count and ranked-bit selection; pointer-width-dependent constants
complexity: word operations plus indexed/scan context; no target timing comparison
rationale: M3 already has fixed 64-bit words and Fenwick rank/select; Swift UInt width and shifts cannot be translated mechanically; concurrent atomic semantics differ

pattern: masked partial words and directional overlap-aware bit copies
complexity: O(number of touched words); boundary merge costs; unmeasured on target
rationale: Qualify 0/63/64/65 endpoints and both overlap directions before any replacement; preserve sparse page ownership and JNI range/lifetime contracts

pattern: hash buckets store offsets into separate element storage; ordered identity is array order
complexity: hash lookup depends on load/collisions; interior dense deletion can require shifted offsets
rationale: Compare packed offset storage against existing stable slot and link lanes; Java live entries/reversed views/null/equality/iterator epochs must remain authoritative

pattern: item and child occupancy bitmaps with compressed node storage and shared-copy mutation
complexity: hash-trie depth and collision-node costs; persistent node allocation differs from flat lanes
rationale: No admitted persistent-map consumer in this pass; Swift TreeDictionary is hash ordered, not a Java sorted map; preserve current mutable/CAS owner contracts

pattern: array min-max heap exposes both extremes; unordered traversal only
complexity: O(log n) insertion/removal; O(1) min/max; target owner is a binary min-heap
rationale: No target double-ended-priority requirement; changing heap layout can alter observable iterator order; retain incumbent min-heap

pattern: blocked B-tree under UnstableSortedCollections; versioned indices
complexity: roughly O(log n) operations plus node shifts; cache/memory tradeoff unmeasured
rationale: Experimental source is a candidate only; not a filtered/live/sorted wrapper donor; Java Comparator/null/range-view/callback/split contracts remain locked

pattern: uniquely owned noncopyable arrays with geometric growth and borrowed spans
complexity: amortized O(1) append; O(n) resize; ownership is enforced by Swift type system
rationale: Reuse existing M3 dynamic arrays; do not add copy-on-write/ARC/borrow semantics to Java aliases or retain JNI pointers across calls
